items.title: The partition is resolved and then ignored — nothing asks whether a service exists in the running partition
items.why_open: apps/web/src/lib/cell-context.ts:44 defines `Partition = "aws" | "aws-us-gov" | "aws-cn"` and :109-111 validates AWS_PARTITION, but the only two consumers of cellContext() read `.region` and nothing else: apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts:34 (`const region = cellContext().region`) and apps/web/src/lib/s3.ts:14 (`new S3Client({ region: cellContext().region })`). A grep for govcloud/aws-us-gov/aws-cn/partition across apps, packages and infrastructure finds no availability matrix anywhere. So a cell deployed with AWS_PARTITION=aws-cn or aws-us-gov still reports `aiConfigured() === true` on the strength of an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and posts tenant content to the commercial api.anthropic.com endpoint — the abstraction resolves the partition and then pretends every service exists in it, which is exactly what the requirement forbids. The model allowlist is region-aware (`modelIsAllowed(configured, region)`, apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts:46) but partition-blind.
items.smallest_real_change: Add apps/web/src/lib/partition-services.ts holding one explicit matrix — `PARTITION_SERVICES: Record<Partition, ReadonlySet<ServiceId>>` over the services this app actually reaches (`s3`, `anthropic-public-api`) — plus `serviceAvailableIn(service, partition)` and `requireService(service)` which throws a named PartitionServiceError quoting the partition and the service. Declare `anthropic-public-api` as commercial-only (it is a public-internet SaaS endpoint, not a partition service) and s3 as present in all three. Wire it into ai.ts by making `aiConfigured()` return false when the running partition does not offer `anthropic-public-api` — that single edit propagates to both real callers, apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:54 and apps/web/src/app/api/ai/draft/route.ts:36, which already have honest degraded paths (sources-only, 503) — and into s3.ts as a `requireService("s3")` on client construction. Test: with AWS_PARTITION=aws-cn and a key set, aiConfigured() is false and the chat route returns sources without prose; mutate by removing the partition check from aiConfigured() — the test must fail.

items.title: The session engine with absolute/idle expiry, rotation and inventory is never wired to the app's actual session
items.why_open: Ledger marks this PASS citing packages/identity/src/session.ts, but `grep -rn '@tenure/identity' apps/web/src` shows the app imports only `reviseMembership`, `SIGN_IN_FAILED_MESSAGE`, `accessState`, `membershipLiveness` and `seatState` — `sessionCookie`, `checkSession`/`sessionLiveness`, `rotateSession`, `sessionInventory`, `revokeSessions`, `checkCsrf` and `cookieProblems` (packages/identity/src/index.ts:41,114,251-263) have zero consumers. The real session is apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:28 — `session: { strategy: 'jwt' }` with no `maxAge` and no `updateAge`, i.e. NextAuth's default 30-day SLIDING window: a token used daily never hits an absolute limit, which is exactly the loophole session.ts:232-235 documents the absolute clock as existing to close. The jwt/session callbacks at auth.ts:72-80 copy `token.sub` and nothing else — no `authAt`, no absolute expiry check, no tenant binding.
items.smallest_real_change: In apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts, extract the callbacks into an exported `const sessionCallbacks` (so they are directly testable) and pass it as `callbacks`. Set `session: { strategy: 'jwt', maxAge: IDLE_SECONDS, updateAge: … }` for the idle clock. In `jwt({token,user})`, stamp `token.authAt = Date.now()` on the sign-in call (the one where `user` is present) and on every subsequent call evaluate the absolute clock with `checkSession` from `@tenure/identity` against `{ expiresAt: authAt + ABSOLUTE_SECONDS }`; return `null` when it reports ABSOLUTE_EXPIRED so NextAuth drops the session, and re-stamp `authAt` only on a fresh authentication, never on use. Test in apps/web/src/lib/auth-session-lifetime.test.ts by invoking the exported callbacks: a token stamped now survives; one stamped past the absolute window returns null; calling the callback repeatedly without a `user` never moves `authAt` forward. Mutation to prove: re-stamp `authAt` on every call and confirm the 'does not slide' + expiry tests fail. HONEST SCOPE: this closes absolute/idle expiry only. Session inventory and immediate server-side revocation need a persisted session table (a new model in apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma plus a migration) and are BLOCKED_EXTERNAL on this host — an operator would run `docker run -d --name tenure-pg -e POSTGRES_USER=tenure -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=tenure -e POSTGRES_DB=tenure -p 5433:5432 postgres:16`, `export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://tenure:tenure@localhost:5433/tenure"`, `cd apps/web && npx prisma migrate dev` — so that half must not be claimed in the same change.

items.title: Read-time authorization after retrieval in the shared search corpus
items.why_open: The corpus that feeds `/search`, `/api/search` and the AI prompt re-authorizes exactly one of its five row types after retrieval. `apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:53-63` calls `canSeeMemoryCard(ctx, m, org)` for memory records — but the approvals loop at `:78-88` has NO `if (!org) continue` guard (the memory, document and event loops all do, at `:55`, `:66`, `:91`), so an approval whose organization is not in the caller's visible org set is still pushed with its full title and description, reached via the unscoped `{ submittedById: userId }` OR branch at `:44`. Separately, `Document.sensitivity` exists in the schema (`apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:667`, `@default("standard")`) and is referenced nowhere in `apps/web/src` — a grep for `sensitivity` across the whole app returns zero hits — so a document's classification label is authorization metadata that no read path consults, and every document's title + description enters the corpus and the model prompt regardless of it. `search-data.itest.ts` only proves cross-tenant separation for memory + documents and needs Postgres; neither gap is covered.
items.smallest_real_change: Add a pure, kernel-free `authorizeRetrieved(row, visibility)` to `search.ts` — it takes the already-fetched row's `{organizationId, sensitivity?}` plus the caller's `{visibleOrgIds:Set<string>, maxSensitivity}` and returns a boolean — so it is unit-testable without a database (this is why it goes in `search.ts` and not `search-data.ts`, which is `server-only` and imports `db`). Then in `search-data.ts`: add `sensitivity: true` to the document `select`, and route all four non-memory loops through `authorizeRetrieved` — which fixes the missing `if (!org) continue` in the approvals loop as a consequence rather than as a one-off patch, and makes the sensitivity label load-bearing for the first time. Tests in `search.test.ts`: a row whose org is absent from `visibleOrgIds` is refused; a `sensitivity:'restricted'` document is refused for a caller at `standard` and allowed at `restricted`; a `standard` document in a visible org is allowed. Mutation: make `authorizeRetrieved` return `true` unconditionally — both refusal assertions must fail. Note the file overlap with GE-092-004 (`search.ts`, `search-data.ts`): these two should be sequenced in one agent, not run in parallel. No Postgres needed.

items.title: Append-only application audit — nothing makes AuditEvent append-only, and 36 of 39 writers bypass the validated record builder
items.why_open: `AuditEvent` is classified only as TENANT_SCOPED (apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/registry.ts:33), so apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/scope-args.ts:113-124 happily scopes-and-permits `update`, `updateMany`, `delete`, `deleteMany` and `upsert` on it — the chokepoint filters the audit trail by tenant and then lets you rewrite or erase it. There is no append-only guard anywhere: grep for `append-only`/`appendOnly` across apps/web/src returns nothing, and the app runs as the RDS master/table owner (apps/web/scripts/entrypoint.sh composes DATABASE_URL from DB_CREDS), so there is no GRANT-level backstop either. Separately, `buildAuditRecord` from `@tenure/audit` — which validates the record shape and redacts by field sensitivity — has exactly two callers (apps/web/src/lib/admin/guard.ts:2 and apps/web/src/lib/provisioning/reconcile.ts:1) while there are 36 hand-assembled `db.auditEvent.create(...)` call sites that go nowhere near it (e.g. apps/web/src/app/api/documents/[id]/content/route.ts:52-62), and none of them records before/after, a change digest, a policy/config version, a represented actor, or a prior hash. Registry status FAIL, ledger: null (registry:4303-4309).
items.smallest_real_change: Two pieces, both inside apps/web and neither needing a migration. (1) `apps/web/src/lib/audit-append-only.ts`: a small Prisma `$extends` that throws on `update|updateMany|delete|deleteMany|upsert` for model `AuditEvent`, attached in apps/web/src/lib/db.ts alongside `tenancyExtension()`. Unlike the tenancy extension this ships in enforce mode from day one — the application has no legitimate audit-mutation call site (the single hit is an .itest teardown), so there is nothing to migrate. (2) `apps/web/src/lib/audit-record.ts`: one `recordAuditEvent()` helper that builds through `@tenure/audit`'s `buildAuditRecord` and stores the extra GE-063-001 fields — represented actor, seat, before/after change digest, policy/config version, prior hash — in the EXISTING `metadata Json` column (schema.prisma `AuditEvent.metadata Json @default("{}")`), chaining `priorHash` off the tenant's last event inside the same transaction. Migrate the 36 call sites to it. Mutation to prove the guard bites: remove `"deleteMany"` from the refused-operation set → the test asserting `db.auditEvent.deleteMany({})` rejects fails. CROSS-AREA NOTE: this edits apps/web/src/lib/db.ts, which the tenancy work also touches; serialize with whoever owns lib/tenancy/** rather than editing concurrently.

items.title: Notification consent / opt-out is stored but never honoured
items.why_open: `NotificationPreference` (userId, channel, enabled) exists in the schema at C:/Users/satvi/Tenure-Parent/apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:929-940 and in the applied baseline migration (migrations/20260730000000_baseline/migration.sql:580,830), but a repo-wide grep for `notificationPreference` across apps/, packages/, tools/, tests/ returns ZERO hits — nothing reads or writes it. C:/Users/satvi/Tenure-Parent/apps/web/src/lib/notify.ts:5-19 `notifyUsers` dedupes ids and excludes self, then calls `db.notification.createMany` for every remaining user unconditionally. Nine real callers depend on it (approvals/actions.ts, calendar/actions.ts, feed/actions.ts, messages/actions.ts, orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts, orgs/[slug]/members/actions.ts, admin/actions.ts, api/jobs/reminders/route.ts, lib/calendar-write.ts), so a user who has opted out of IN_APP still receives everything.
items.smallest_real_change: In `notifyUsers`, before the `createMany`, read `db.notificationPreference.findMany({ where: { userId: { in: ids }, channel: 'IN_APP' } })` and drop any recipient whose row exists with `enabled: false` (absent row = enabled, so no backfill and no migration is needed — the column is already in the baseline). Return early when the filtered set is empty. Add `notify.test.ts` with `@/lib/db` jest-mocked the way apps/web/src/app/api/ai/ai-kill-switch.test.ts mocks its boundaries: assert an opted-out user is absent from the `createMany` payload while an opted-in and an unknown user are present. Mutation proof: delete the filter line and the opted-out assertion must fail.

items.title: Hard/soft conflict engine with explainable rule, override authority and an audited decision
items.why_open: The classifier exists but the governance around it does not. apps/web/src/lib/calendar.ts:47-90 `detectConflicts` returns `{conflictWithEventId, severity, reason}` where `reason` is an interpolated English sentence — there is no rule identifier and no record of which inputs fired it, so nothing downstream can name the rule, test it by name, or show a stable explanation. apps/web/src/lib/calendar-write.ts:296-350 shows the missing half: after a drag-to-reschedule it computes `const hard = conflicts.filter(c => c.severity === 'HARD')`, writes the event ANYWAY (the `db.event.update` at line 294 already happened), records only `hardConflicts: hard.length` in the audit metadata, and notifies presidents. There is no override capability check, no explicit override decision by the actor, and no `ConflictOverridden` audit row — a HARD conflict is advisory in every path. The authority primitive already exists and is unused here: `event.override` is declared at apps/web/src/lib/admin/capabilities.ts:32,124 and enforced via `requireCapability` at apps/web/src/app/(app)/admin/actions.ts:887.
items.smallest_real_change: (1) In apps/web/src/lib/calendar.ts add a `rule` discriminant to `DetectedConflict` — `'VENUE_DOUBLE_BOOKING' | 'SELF_DOUBLE_BOOKING' | 'AUDIENCE_OVERLAP' | 'SAME_DAY'` — set at each of the four push sites, and carry the inputs that fired it (`{venue, otherStartAt, otherEndAt}`) so the explanation is derived rather than only rendered. (2) New pure module apps/web/src/lib/calendar-conflict-policy.ts: `decideConflictOutcome({conflicts, actorHasOverride, overrideRequested, overrideReason})` returning `{allowed, blockedByRules[], override: null | {rules[], reason}}` — HARD conflicts block unless the actor holds override authority AND explicitly asked with a reason; SOFT/INFORMATIONAL never block. (3) In calendar-write.ts move the `recheckConflicts` call BEFORE the `db.event.update` at line 294, call the policy, return `{error}` when it blocks, and when it allows via override write an `Event.ConflictOverridden` audit row carrying the rule ids and the reason alongside the existing `Event.Rescheduled` row. Test the policy module directly: a HARD conflict with no override authority is blocked; with authority but no explicit request it is still blocked; with both it is allowed and reports the rule ids. Mutation: make `decideConflictOutcome` ignore `actorHasOverride` — the second case must fail.

items.title: Currency precision, rounding and invariant tests for money parsing
items.why_open: C:/Users/satvi/Tenure-Parent/apps/web/src/lib/finance.ts:76 and :93 both round money through binary floating point (`Math.round(value * 100)` / `Math.round(parseFloat(s) * 100)`), and the two branches disagree on the same amount. Verified by running the exact code: `parseMoneyToCents(-0.005)` returns `-0` while `parseMoneyToCents("-0.005")` returns `-1`; `parseMoneyToCents("1.005")` returns 100 (should be 101 half-away-from-zero) and `"0.145"` returns 14 (should be 15). Both branches are live production paths: the number branch is fed by xlsx cell values through `parseBudgetSheet` (finance.ts:233-234, called from src/components/finance/BudgetUpload.tsx:41) and the string branch by FormData in src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts:64,65,125,236,367 — budget lines, ledger postings and reimbursement amounts. Separately the function is asymmetric with its own formatter: it always multiplies by 100, while packages/platform-config/src/money.ts:40-41 divides by `10 ** Intl-resolved exponent`, so parse/format do not round-trip for any currency whose minor unit is not 1/100. src/lib/finance.test.ts:19-36 tests only whole-cent inputs, so none of this is currently caught.
items.smallest_real_change: Rewrite `parseMoneyToCents` to round on the decimal string rather than on a float: normalise the input to a sign + integer part + fraction string, take the currency's minor-unit exponent (default 2) as a parameter, and round half-away-from-zero by inspecting the first dropped digit — never `Math.round(x * 100)`. Normalise `-0` to `0`. Give both entry paths one shared implementation so the number branch stringifies before rounding. Then add invariant tests to finance.test.ts: parse(format(n)) === n over a table of amounts, string and number forms of the same amount agree, half-way values round away from zero in both signs, reversal (`ledgerSignedCents("REIMBURSEMENT", x)` then re-post) nets to zero, and `summarize` totals equal the sum of the lines. Mutation proof: restore `Math.round(parseFloat(s) * 100)` and the sign-agreement and half-way tests must fail.

items.title: An OSE member can approve their own approval request — the no-self-approval control exists in @tenure/authorization and has zero callers in the app
items.why_open: apps/web/src/lib/approvals.ts:77-84 (`workflowRolesFor`) pushes BOTH `requester` and `oseGate` when `isRequester` and `isOse(ctx, institutionId)` are true, and packages/workflow/src/engine.ts:55 filters transitions by `allowedRoles` only — there is no deny/forbid concept. So for a request the actor submitted, `availableActions` at PENDING_OSE returns approve/reject/request_changes for that same actor, and apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:163 gates the write on exactly that list. If the actor is also an ACTIVE club president, approval-definition.ts:52-58 skips the president gate on submit, so one person can carry their own request DRAFT → APPROVED with no second human. packages/authorization/src/controls.ts:116-127 already implements `mayDecide` returning `SELF_APPROVAL`, plus SAME_MAKER, RECUSED and cross-gate four-eyes at :171+ — and grep for it across apps/web/src returns nothing (the only @tenure/authorization imports in apps/web are ROLE_TEMPLATES, lookupRoleTemplate, permission lookups and SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES). apps/web/src/lib/approvals.test.ts (113 lines) has no self-approval assertion.
items.smallest_real_change: In apps/web/src/lib/approvals.ts, make `availableActions` run its result through `mayDecide` from @tenure/authorization for the deciding actions (approve / reject / request_changes), passing `{ raisedByPrincipalId: approval.submittedById, tenantId: approval.institutionId, resourceId: approval.id }` and the actor's id; drop those actions when the outcome is not ok. `submit`/`cancel`/`resubmit` are requester actions and stay. This is the whole fix — actions.ts:163 already enforces membership of the returned list, so there is a real call path. Test in approvals.test.ts: an OSE-Director ctx whose `userId` equals `submittedById` gets `[]` (not `['approve','request_changes','reject']`) at PENDING_OSE, while a different OSE user still gets all three; and the president-gate-skip test at :74 must stay green. Mutation: remove the mayDecide filter and confirm the new assertion fails.

items.title: Redeploy must never rerun destructive seed logic — seed.mjs still issues unscoped deletes with no environment guard, and its own header claims the opposite of the truth
items.why_open: apps/web/scripts/seed.mjs:395 `await db.approvalDelegation.deleteMany({})` — completely unscoped, deletes every approval delegation in the database including the live pilot's customer-created rows. Also :400 (budgetLine), :431 `db.ledgerEntry.deleteMany({ where: { organizationId: consulting.id } })` followed by reposting demo entries, and :500 (document). Nothing in the file refuses to run against production: the only NODE_ENV check is at :78/:103 and it guards *demo login accounts only*, not the deletes. apps/web/scripts/entrypoint.sh already reached the right conclusion in prose ("Seeding is NOT part of starting a server... it issues unscoped deletes to reset test state. Running it on every boot... destroyed live rows while doing it") but still invokes `node scripts/seed.mjs` whenever `SEED_ON_BOOT=true`, so the protection is one environment variable deep and lives outside the script that does the damage. Worse, seed.mjs:1-2 still states "Idempotent pilot seed — safe to run on every container start" — a false claim that the entrypoint directly contradicts. There is no test: apps/web/scripts/db-bootstrap.test.mjs covers the migration planner, nothing covers the seed. Registry status FAIL, ledger: null (registry:5071-5077).
items.smallest_real_change: New pure module `apps/web/scripts/seed-guard.mjs` exporting `decideSeedAllowed({ nodeEnv, databaseUrl, seedDestructive })` → `{ allowed, reason }`, refusing whenever `nodeEnv === "production"` unless `SEED_DESTRUCTIVE === "true"` is explicitly set, and refusing on a `databaseUrl` host that is not localhost/127.0.0.1 while NODE_ENV is unset. Call it as the first statement of `main()` in seed.mjs (apps/web/scripts/seed.mjs:50) and `process.exit(1)` with the reason on refusal. Fix the false header comment at seed.mjs:1-2 to state what entrypoint.sh states — it is a destructive dev/e2e fixture, not a boot-safe idempotent seed. Test in apps/web/scripts/seed-guard.test.mjs (jest `roots` already includes `<rootDir>/scripts`, and `moduleFileExtensions` already includes `mjs`, so this needs no config change). Mutation to prove it bites: flip the production branch to return `{ allowed: true }` → the "refuses in production without the explicit opt-in" case fails. No database required.

items.title: No lint or architecture rule prevents literal colors or raw tokens in product modules
items.why_open: Registry marks GE-143-004 FAIL. apps/web/eslint.config.mjs is fifteen lines and its entire ruleset is `compat.extends("next/core-web-vitals", "next/typescript")` (lines 12-14) — no `rules` block at all, so there is no rule against literal colors, arbitrary spacing/shadow/z-index, unregistered fonts/icons or raw primitive tokens, and no exception mechanism or expiry to speak of. A token system does exist and is enforced only downstream of the fact: apps/web/src/lib/a11y/theme-tokens.ts parses the real `--token` declarations out of app/globals.css for the contrast audit. The drift is already live but still tiny — `grep -rnoE '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}' src/components src/app` returns 8 hits (apps/web/src/components/ai/TenureAIPanel.tsx:121, apps/web/src/components/ui/Avatar.tsx:59, apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx:37-38, apps/web/src/app/apple-icon.tsx:23,26, apps/web/src/app/manifest.ts:15-16), and zero arbitrary Tailwind color values. That is what makes this closable now rather than a cleanup project.
items.smallest_real_change: Add a `rules` entry to apps/web/eslint.config.mjs scoped to `src/components/**` and `src/app/(app)/**` using `no-restricted-syntax` with selectors matching string literals containing `/#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b/`, `rgb(`/`hsl(`, and Tailwind arbitrary-value brackets `[#...]`/`[NNpx]`/`z-[`, each with a message naming the token to use instead. Add a sibling override block that lists the four genuine exceptions (layout.tsx and manifest.ts theme-color meta, apple-icon.tsx's OG-image renderer, Avatar.tsx's deterministic swatch) each carrying an inline `// EXPIRES: YYYY-MM-DD — reason` comment, and a rule-level check that fails on an expired date so the exception process has teeth rather than being prose. Test: a new apps/web/src/lib/a11y/design-token-lint.test.ts that instantiates ESLint's `Linter` with the same rule config and asserts (a) `const c = "#ff0000"` in a product-path fixture reports an error, (b) the same source under `src/app/manifest.ts` does not, (c) an exception comment dated in the past reports. Mutation: delete the `no-restricted-syntax` entry from the config; assertion (a) must fail, then restore. Note the config file sits at apps/web/eslint.config.mjs — confirm it is inside the assigned allowlist before editing, since the ownership section of my brief arrived empty.

items.title: Complete component-state matrix, including no-results, syncing, read-only, pending purge and a geometry-matched skeleton
items.why_open: Registry status FAIL, ledger: null. The existing matrix is real but covers 10 of the 21 named states: SurfaceState (components/ui/states.ts:20-31) is loading, empty, error, permission-denied, stale, conflict, offline, archived, partial, high-risk-confirm. Missing and unrepresentable through StateSurface: no-results (distinct from empty — 'your filter matched nothing' is a different action than 'nothing exists yet'; DEFAULT_COPY at states.ts:178 currently makes empty say 'This is up to date', which is wrong copy for a filtered miss), syncing (distinct from offline — offline says 'Changes will not save', which is the opposite of syncing), read-only, and pending-purge. The geometry-matched skeleton clause has no implementation at all: a grep for skeleton/Skeleton across src/components, src/app and src/lib returns zero hits, so the `loading` state renders a text card rather than layout-preserving geometry.
items.smallest_real_change: Extend SurfaceState with 'no-results', 'syncing', 'read-only' and 'pending-purge', give each an entry in STATE_SEMANTICS (no-results: presentsAsComplete true, retryable false; syncing: role status/polite, presentsAsComplete false, retryable false; read-only: role region/off, presentsAsComplete true; pending-purge: role alert/assertive, tone danger, presentsAsComplete false) and DEFAULT_COPY, plus the matching branches in retryAdvice (states.ts:207-227) so the existing exhaustiveness holds. Add components/ui/Skeleton.tsx taking explicit rows/height so the placeholder occupies the same box the loaded content will, and render it from StateSurface when state === 'loading' and a geometry prop is supplied. The purely interaction-level states (hover/active/focus-visible/selected/disabled) belong to Button/TextField/Select and are out of scope for this table. Mutation proof: a states.test.ts case asserting retryAdvice('no-results').offerRetry is false and that DEFAULT_COPY['no-results'].detail differs from empty's; collapse no-results back onto empty and confirm it goes red.

items.title: Chart API must give a category deterministic colour identity, independent of its rank
items.why_open: components/charts/palette.ts:8-11 states colours "are assigned to entities in FIXED SLOT ORDER and never cycled or repainted when a filter changes the series count: the hue follows the entity, not its rank" — the code does the opposite. `slotColor(i)` (palette.ts:28) is keyed by array index, DonutChart.tsx:59 passes the loop index (`color: d.color ?? slotColor(i)`), and panels/ReportsAnalytics.tsx:109-111 builds `memoryData` by sorting the counts descending, inside a `useMemo` keyed on the RangeFilter `range`. Concrete failure: with range=year PLAYBOOK outranks CONTACT and takes --chart-1; switch to range=term where CONTACT outranks PLAYBOOK and the two swap hues, so the legend of the same donut means something different in each view. The comment claim is what is false here, and it should be corrected by making the code true.
items.smallest_real_change: Add `slotsForKeys(keys: readonly string[]): Map<string,string>` to palette.ts, assigning the eight slots by canonical (lexicographic) key order rather than by arrival order, so the map is independent of both input order and set size for the keys it shares. Give `DonutDatum` an optional `key` defaulting to `label`, and have DonutChart build the map once and read `map.get(d.key ?? d.label)` in place of `slotColor(i)` at lines 59 and 118. Test: the same four category keys in count-descending and count-ascending order, and with different values, must yield the identical colour for each key. Mutation: restore `slotColor(i)` in DonutChart and the equality assertion fails.

items.title: Test Sankey at small, medium, large, and pathological graph sizes; aggregate or switch representation before labels become unreadable
items.why_open: apps/web/src/components/charts/SankeyChart.tsx:140 `function computeLayout(...)` is module-private and has NO test file (no SankeyChart.test.ts exists), while the component ships to two production surfaces — apps/web/src/components/charts/panels/ReportsAnalytics.tsx:202 and apps/web/src/components/finance/PortfolioSankey.tsx:19. There is no aggregation and no representation switch anywhere in the file: node bands are clamped by `Math.max(3, (through.get(id) ?? 0) * scale)` (line 194) so once a layer holds more than plotH/(3+nodeGap) nodes the stacked total exceeds plotH and bands silently overlap; ribbon thickness has no floor at all (`l.value * scale`, lines 218/228) and degenerates to sub-pixel hairlines; and every node's label is rendered unconditionally at fontSize 11 (lines 116-131) with no reference to its band height.
items.smallest_real_change: Export `computeLayout` and give it a stated capacity rule: per layer, keep the top-K nodes by throughput where K = floor((plotH + nodeGap) / (MIN_NODE_H + nodeGap)), fold the remainder into one aggregated `Other (n)` node and re-point their links at it; floor ribbon thickness at MIN_RIBBON_H; and mark each positioned node `showLabel = h >= LABEL_LINE_H` so suppressed labels survive only in the existing <title>. New SankeyChart.test.ts drives the pure function at 3 nodes, ~20, ~200, and pathological (one layer of 500 equal-value nodes; plus zero-value links and a self-link) asserting: stacked band totals never exceed plotH, no returned band or ribbon is below its minimum, an `Other` node appears exactly when K is exceeded and its value equals the folded sum, and every showLabel node is at least LABEL_LINE_H tall. Mutation: delete the fold and return all nodes — the ~200 and pathological cases blow the plotH assertion and fail.

items.title: Revocation of a membership, assignment, delegation or policy must invalidate cached decisions immediately
items.why_open: packages/authorization/src/service.ts caches decisions and bounds them only by DATED facts: `validUntil` (:139-208) collects `effectiveFrom`/`effectiveTo` from memberships, grants, delegations and relationships, and returns null when none is in the future (:206) — i.e. cached until eviction. A revocation is not a date change: deleting a role assignment, ending a membership out of band or removing a delegation moves no `effectiveTo` the cache has already read, so a decision taken before the revocation keeps returning ALLOW. The only escape hatches are a `PolicyRevision` id change (:252-256), which covers configuration edits and not per-principal facts, and `invalidate()` (:277-279), which is all-or-nothing and has no caller anywhere in the tree (grep finds only its definition and the re-export at index.ts:187). REVIEW-FINDINGS §14 names this same defect from the other side — the per-membership `authz_version` fan-out is 'never specified' — and the review wins over the spec.
items.smallest_real_change: Add an optional `subjectRevision?: (request: AuthorizationRequest) => string` to `AuthorizationServiceOptions` (service.ts:210-216), read on EVERY authorize call exactly as `revision()` already is, and fold its value into `decisionKey` (:107-118) so a bumped stamp is a structural miss rather than a hoped-for eviction; plus `invalidatePrincipal(tenantId, principalId)` on `AuthorizationService` that drops just that principal's entries, which requires the key's tenant/principal prefix to be a documented, parseable part of the format. Test in service.test.ts: authorize (ALLOW, cached false), authorize again (cached true), then revoke by removing the grant from the world AND bumping the subject stamp — the next call must be `cached: false` and DENY; and the same revocation WITHOUT the stamp bump must still be served stale, which is the fact that makes the stamp load-bearing. Mutation: drop the stamp from `decisionKey` — the post-revocation DENY assertion goes red. Honest caveat: `authorizationService` currently has no apps/web caller (only the package index re-exports it), so this hardens the platform boundary rather than a live request path; wiring apps/web onto the service is a larger, separate change.

items.title: @tenure/audit builds records but cannot verify, detect gaps, project, export, retain or hold them
items.why_open: packages/audit contains exactly three files (record.ts, index.ts, audit.test.ts). packages/audit/src/index.ts:21-33 exports precisely four things: `AuditRecordError`, `REDACTED`, `buildAuditRecord`, `redactMetadata`. `AuditRecord` (record.ts:73-87) has no sequence number, no previous-record hash and no record hash, so tamper-detection and gap-detection have nothing to work from. grep for retention/legalHold/hashChain across apps/web/src/lib returns no audit-related hit — the only audit surface, apps/web/src/app/(app)/admin/audit/page.tsx:58-60, is a raw `db.auditEvent.findMany({... take: 200})` with a text filter: no verification, no export, no retention, no legal hold. Registry has `ledger: null` for GE-063-004 and the id appears nowhere in the global-engine ledger, so nothing claims it done.
items.smallest_real_change: Add `sequence: number` and `previousHash: string | null` to `AuditRecordInput`/`AuditRecord` and compute a `recordHash` over the frozen record in `buildAuditRecord` (record.ts:196) using the same node:crypto sha256 the releases package already uses. New `verify.ts` exporting `verifyChain(records)` -> `{ok, tampered: {sequence, expectedHash, actualHash}[], gaps: {after, before, missing}[]}` (gap = a break in the per-tenant sequence, which is precisely what an append-only log cannot otherwise reveal) and `projectForQuery(records, {sensitivity})` that re-applies `redactMetadata` on read so an export cannot leak what the write redacted. New `retention.ts` exporting `applyRetention(records, {retainDays, asOf}, holds: LegalHold[])` returning `{expire, retain, heldBack}` where a record matching any active hold is NEVER in `expire`. All pure functions over arrays — no database, so this is fully doable on this host. Mutation test that proves it: make `applyRetention` ignore the holds array and assert the 'a record under legal hold is never expired' test fails; separately flip one byte of a record's metadata and assert `verifyChain` reports it tampered. CROSS-AREA: the chain only becomes real once the two production writers persist `sequence`/`previousHash` — apps/web/src/lib/admin/guard.ts:2 and apps/web/src/lib/provisioning/reconcile.ts:1 both call `buildAuditRecord`. Keep the new fields optional at first so those call sites keep compiling, and report the persistence step as the cross-area dependency it is.

items.title: Cell admission is a binary full/not-full test — no quota thresholds, no shard/new-cell/vend recommendation, no block before exhaustion
items.why_open: `packages/provisioning/src/cell-registry.ts:260` is the entire capacity rule: `healthy.filter((c) => c.capacity.tenants < c.capacity.maxTenants)`, refusing with `no-capacity` only once the last slot is literally consumed. `CellCapacity` (`:58-69`) carries only `tenants` and `maxTenants` — no reserve, no warning threshold. A grep across `packages/provisioning/src` finds no `threshold`, `headroom`, `shard`, `vend` or `recommend`, so none of 'quota thresholds', 'shard/new-cell/account-vend recommendations' or 'onboarding block before exhaustion' exists. The path is live: `apps/system-studio/src/lib/cells.ts:112` -> `apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/actions.ts:240`, which already renders `placement.reason` as a form problem.
items.smallest_real_change: Add `reserve` and `warnAt` to `CellCapacity` and a `FleetAdmission` result to `choosePlacement`: filter on `tenants < maxTenants - reserve` (so onboarding stops before exhaustion rather than at it), add a `no-headroom` refusal distinct from `no-capacity`, and return a `recommendation` of `'none' | 'shard-cell' | 'add-cell' | 'vend-account'` derived deterministically from how many healthy in-residency cells are above `warnAt` (all above -> add-cell; none in residency at all but healthy cells elsewhere -> vend-account). CROSS-AREA DEPENDENCY: the new refusal reason renders correctly only if `apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/actions.ts:245-262` gets a branch for it — its ternary chain currently falls through to 'Every cell is at capacity', which would be wrong copy for a headroom block. If apps/system-studio is not mine, I stop at the package boundary and this needs the system-studio owner. Mutation proof: change the filter back to `< maxTenants` and the test asserting a cell at maxTenants-1 with reserve 1 is refused with `no-headroom` must fail.

items.title: Signed deployment manifest with the named digests
items.why_open: packages/provisioning/src/execute.ts:395-422 produces a DeploymentManifest, and the doc comments at lines 22-27 and 346 say it is "signed". It is not signed by anything — `digest: sha(body)` at line 421 is an unkeyed SHA-256, there is no key, no signature field, and apps/web/src/lib/provisioning/reconcile.ts:117-140 "verifies" by recomputing the same unkeyed hash, which proves nothing about origin. So the word "signed" in both files is a false claim. On content, the item names release/config/schema/migration/resource/test/evidence/rollback digests; the body (lines 404-419) carries manifestDigest, configurationChecksum, modules, blueprintId, schemaVersion, configKeys, evidenceDigest and serving — no releaseId or release digest (packages/releases/src/release.ts computes one and nothing links it), no migration digest, no provisioned-resource digest, no verification/test digest, and no rollback target digest, so a cell cannot tell which prior artifact this one rolls back to.
items.smallest_real_change: Two separable pieces, both inside packages/provisioning. (1) Correct the claim: replace "signs"/"signed" in the execute.ts header and the DeploymentManifest doc comment with "digests", and say plainly that origin authenticity is not yet established. (2) Add the missing digests to the digest-covered body from data the run already has rather than inventing fields: `releaseDigest` from the release identity the manifest cites, and `migrationDigest` / `resourceDigest` / `testDigest` / `rollbackDigest` derived from the `StepEvidence.digest` already emitted by the MIGRATING, PROVISIONING and VERIFYING steps plus the previous manifest's digest passed in `meta`. Test in provisioning.test.ts: changing only the VERIFYING step's evidence digest must change the manifest `digest`; mutation = leave testDigest out of `body`, the test fails because the two manifests hash identically. This is compatible with the cell without touching it — apps/web/src/lib/provisioning/reconcile.ts:117 destructures `{ digest, ...body }` and canonicalises generically, so added fields verify. Cross-area dependency, not to be fixed here: a real signature (KMS-asymmetric or Ed25519) needs a `signature` field checked in apps/web/src/lib/provisioning/reconcile.ts and a key source in apps/system-studio.
